basics.name: Marcelo Rondon
basics.label: Product Designer, Human-Centered AI Systems
basics.summary: Product designer building human-centered AI systems that augment creative workflows without replacing human judgment. I bridge design and engineering by turning real workflows into working tools with bounded automation, editable states, validation, accessibility, and clear handoff intent. Recent work includes Ghosted, an AI-assisted job-application product, and Daybreak, a local-first Mac and iPhone planner with a typed, receipt-backed agent layer.

work.name: Asheville Dispensary
highlights: Own product design across web, print, and packaging, anchored by a Figma design system that keeps the brand coherent as the product line grows.
Designed and built an internal asset-management tool in React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS that gives marketing and operations one place to find, manage, and preserve brand assets.
Design and ship reusable UI components into WordPress through custom PHP and JavaScript plugins, closing the gap between mockups and production.
Partner with marketing and operations to turn ambiguous requests into scoped, shipped product surfaces.

work.name: VegAvengers Marketing
highlights: Designed and shipped a responsive discovery experience with flexible search across VegFests, animal sanctuaries, locations, dates, months, and changing event states.
Evolved the product into a hybrid Astro and Payload architecture: prerendered editorial pages, live resource-search APIs, and a headless CMS backed by Postgres with media in Cloudflare R2.

Defined debounced, selective rebuild policies plus fixture and Astro DB fallback paths so content changes avoid unnecessary deploys and the public experience degrades safely if Payload is unavailable.

work.name: Cello.Design

projects.name: Ghosted
projects.description: Designed and built an AI-assisted job-application workspace — from a Go terminal prototype to a shipped web product where deterministic code does the work and one bounded model call writes the prose.
highlights: Rewrote a Go TUI prototype into a live Next.js/TypeScript web product with posting capture, deterministic fit scoring, and ATS-validated PDF export

Designed the 'minimum viable intelligence' architecture: code parses, scores, and validates; the model only writes prose, checked against a 180-word cap, a banned-phrase list, and CV-grounded honesty flags
Built a triage review UI (accept, reject, edit) and targeted revision so generated material is edited from, never pasted over
Shipped to real testers on an invite-gated shared subscription, folding feedback into a synchronous double-fire guard and tighter layouts
Backed by 744 tests across a pure-TypeScript core and a Next.js app

projects.name: Daybreak
projects.description: Designed and built a local-first personal planning product for Mac and iPhone that combines a deterministic planning engine with agent-assisted adjustments while keeping the plan editable and the user in control.
highlights: Shipped a shared SwiftUI and SwiftData app for macOS and iPhone with private CloudKit sync, without a product account or hosted application server
Separated a pure, testable planning engine from the app layer so generated day plans obey explicit schedule, ownership, and local-day boundary rules
Defined typed UI-agent parity contracts so agent-accessible actions match the product grammar, emit auditable receipts, and leave destructive or external actions behind explicit safety exclusions
Kept automated planning inspectable and editable: people can review, move, defer, or remove Daybreak-owned blocks while source-owned calendar meetings remain protected
Dogfooded the product against real planning and sync failures, turning trust problems into tested product rules across Mac and iPhone
